sources.title: Effect of annealing in eutectic high-entropy alloy superconductor NbScTiZr
Superconducting properties of eutectic high-entropy alloy superconductor NbScTiZr

methods.summary: Arc melting in argon on a water-cooled copper hearth; nominal Nb:Sc:Ti:Zr atomic ratio 1:1:1:1. Heat treatment at 400, 800 or 1000 °C for four days in an evacuated quartz tube.
Arc melting in argon on a water-cooled copper hearth; nominal Nb:Sc:Ti:Zr atomic ratio 1:1:1:1. Annealing at 400, 600, 800 or 1000 °C for four days in an evacuated quartz tube.

Figure 3(a) identifies Tc at ac-susceptibility diamagnetic onset. The ac setup uses 5 Oe at 800 Hz over 3–20 K. Resistivity zero is separately confirmed. The Table 1 values remain independent source expressions.

Cu-Kα XRD with least-squares lattice parameter evaluation. The source attributes chemical composition to EDX coupled with field-emission SEM and cites the preceding study. Table 1 prints composition coefficients without an explicit composition unit.

The text describes refined Tc from upper-critical-field analysis and M(T) diamagnetic-onset datasets analyzed with WHH. Resistivity transition onset yields a separate WHH channel. Table 2 values retain that Hc2-analysis context without assigning calorimetric midpoint or a common criterion across all probes.

The source extrapolates Hc1(0) with a Ginzburg–Landau model. Coherence length is calculated from Hc2(0); penetration depth uses Hc1(0) and the matching coherence-length channel; κ is their ratio. These are source-derived estimates, not direct length measurements or electron–phonon coupling.

Normal-state C/T versus T² fitting yields γel and β with both bcc and hcp contributions. Four annealed specimens receive exponential electronic-specific-heat gap fits plus a residual γ term attributed by the authors to hcp. The normalized heat-jump analysis explicitly uses transition midpoint Tc; this does not assign midpoint to the whole Table 2 Tc row.
Vickers indentation is measured on polished surfaces with a 2.94 N load for ten seconds. Parentheses in source hardness and lattice values are preserved without interpreting uncertainties.

The source obtains phase volume fractions from SEM images and phase compositions from EDX. Its Table 1 lists composition-derived valence electron concentration separately. These are source phase reports, not superconducting volume fractions or catalogued atomic models.

gap_fits.as_cast_reason: The paper excludes the as-cast sample from these superconducting specific-heat fits; transition broadening prevents evaluating its gap ratio.
gap_fits.interpretation_scope: Source fit and model-ratio estimates. Author discussion of possible strong coupling does not establish a global pairing classification or electron–phonon λ.

limitations: Source sample labels describe preparation groups, not typed catalogue sample or state IDs.
Annealing temperature and four-day hold are processing conditions, not superconducting measurement conditions. As-cast is not represented as a 0 °C anneal.
A formula match, a shared author group or a citation does not establish the same physical specimen across the papers.
Original PDF and full derived text remain private; metadata publishes source values, paraphrased context and hash-only locations.
No pressure value is supplied from missing source fields, and zero-temperature fitted values do not establish measurements at 0 K.
No scientific acceptance, human gold benchmark, canonical promotion, new DFT or ML permission is created.
